incidents: Patient in bed 14 got up alone at about 03:00 to use the toilet, lost balance beside the bed and sat down on the floor. Bed alarm had been switched off after the previous round. No injury found on review.
Helped back to bed, checked by doctor, family informed, bed alarm switched back on.
Unwitnessed slide to floor beside bed, no injury
Elderly patient walking to the bathroom with a frame slipped on a wet patch near the sluice room and grazed her elbow. The floor had been mopped but no wet-floor sign was in place.
First aid for graze, floor dried, sign placed, incident discussed at handover.
Slip on unsigned wet floor causing elbow graze
Post-operative patient tried to stand without help after receiving pain relief and dizzy episode, caught by a passing healthcare assistant and lowered to the chair.
Observations repeated and normal, call bell explained again.
Dizzy post-operative patient lowered safely by staff
Patient fell in the shared bathroom when the shower chair slid on the tiles. Small bruise on left hip, no fracture on examination.
Reviewed by doctor, shower chair removed from use, tiles checked by facilities.
Shower chair slipped on tiles causing hip bruise
Night nurse noticed a confused patient climbing over bed rails and reached him before he lowered himself. No fall occurred.
Patient returned to bed, low bed requested, one-to-one observation arranged.
Confused patient intercepted climbing over bed rails
Patient fell on the way to the bathroom and cut her forehead on the bedside locker, needing four sutures in Emergency. Call bell was within reach but she did not want to disturb staff.
Wound sutured, neurological observations for 24 hours, family informed.
A visitor noticed a patient on the floor beside bed 21 and called for help. Patient reported sliding from the edge of the bed while reaching for a phone. No pain or injury.
Full assessment with no injury found, phone placed within reach.
Patient slid from bed edge reaching for phone
Patient waiting for results stood up from a trolley with the side rail down and fell, bruising the right knee. Trolley rails had been lowered for a procedure and not raised again.
Examined and X-ray clear, rails raised, trolley checklist reminder sent to team.
Trolley rails left down after procedure, patient fell
Toddler climbed the cot side while the parent was out of the room and slid down the mattress end onto a padded mat. Child checked and well.
Child checked by paediatrician, cot sides locked, parent counselled.
Toddler climbed cot side onto padded mat
Patient on a new blood pressure tablet was found sitting on the floor next to the commode at 22:40. He said his legs went weak. Observations stable.
Doctor review, medication timing reviewed with pharmacist, commode moved next to bed.
Weak legs after new tablet, found sitting by commode
Healthcare assistant caught a patient who tripped on a loose oxygen tube across the walkway when returning from the toilet.
Tubing rerouted behind the bed, patient reassessed for falls risk.
Trip on loose oxygen tubing caught by staff member
Patient slipped on a spill of juice beside bed 3 and bruised her wrist. Spill was reported by the patient 10 minutes earlier and not yet cleaned.
Wrist checked, spill cleaned, housekeeping informed.
Slip on reported spill left uncleaned for 10 minutes
Patient fainted while sitting in the CT waiting area after fasting since the night before and was lowered to the floor by a porter. Recovered after a sugary drink.
Observations and blood sugar normal, doctor review, fasting advice improved on appointment letter.
Fasting patient fainted in waiting area and was lowered safely
Nurse picked up insulin 100 units/ml in a pen that looked the same as the long-acting pen and noticed the label before drawing up. The pens were stored in the same tray.
Pens separated into labelled trays, pharmacy asked to relabel.
Look-alike insulin pens noticed before administration
Morning blood pressure tablet was given twice, once by the night nurse at 06:00 and again at 08:30, because the first administration was not signed on the chart. Blood pressure stayed within range.
Observations for four hours with no change, doctor informed, family told.

Potassium infusion ran at twice the prescribed rate for about 40 minutes after the pump was set to a different rate at handover. Potassium rose and required monitoring and treatment before returning to normal.
Infusion stopped, repeat bloods, cardiac monitoring for 12 hours, family informed.
Infusion pump programmed at double rate after handover
Pharmacist reviewing the order noticed a paediatric dose written in milligrams per kilogram using the adult weight and corrected it before supply.
Prescription corrected, prescriber informed and weight field made mandatory.
Paediatric dose miscalculated and corrected by pharmacist
Patient received a metformin box labelled for another patient with a similar surname. Error found by the patient at home and exchanged the same afternoon. No tablets taken.
Correct medication supplied, apology given, counter checking process reviewed.
Wrong patient's medication handed over at pharmacy counter
Nurse found that an antibiotic dose due at 14:00 had not been charted for a penicillin-allergic patient who had a red allergy band. She stopped and queried the prescription before giving it.
Prescription changed to a non-penicillin option, allergy field on chart rechecked.
Penicillin prescribed despite allergy band, stopped by nurse
Oxytocin infusion bag was hung with a label showing the wrong concentration, noticed during the double-check, but the infusion had already run for five minutes at a low rate.
Infusion stopped, correct bag hung, mother and baby monitored without effect.
Wrong concentration label on oxytocin bag
Patient with a documented eggs sensitivity was given a propofol-containing sedation. Mild rash and itching developed and settled after an antihistamine.
Antihistamine given, allergy record updated and discussed with anaesthetist.
Mild rash after sedation in patient with recorded sensitivity
Oral paracetamol syrup was measured with a 10 ml syringe instead of the 5 ml syringe, giving a dose that was within safe limits but above the chart. Child was well after observation.
Doctor informed, observations unchanged, syringe sizes labelled in the clean utility room.
Slightly high paracetamol dose from wrong syringe size
A technician spotted that a heparin lock flush syringe was stored in the same drawer as saline flushes and swapped them before use.
Heparin and saline flushes stored together
Controlled drug count did not match at the change of shift. After a search the missing ampoule was found recorded on the wrong page of the register. No drug was lost.
Register corrected, both nurses re-signed, quality team informed.
Controlled drug count mismatch due to register entry on wrong page
Blood sample labelled for bed 8 was noticed by the lab technician to have a request form for a different patient. Sample was rejected and redrawn.
Redraw at the bedside with the wristband check, staff reminded of two-identifier rule.
Sample and request form mismatch rejected by lab

Two patients with the same first name were called at the same time and the wrong patient started to get ready for a chest X-ray. The radiographer checked the date of birth and stopped before exposure.
Right patient imaged, same-name alert flag raised in the booking list.
Same-name patients almost swapped before chest X-ray
Patient was missing a wristband after a dressing change and a nurse about to give a unit of blood caught the omission at bedside check. New band printed and confirmed with the patient and the notes.
Wristband replaced and verified with two staff before the transfusion.
Missing wristband identified at pre-transfusion check
A discharge letter with another patient's medication list was handed to a patient at the desk. The patient noticed the wrong name and returned it unopened to the nurse.
Letter replaced, information governance team notified.
Wrong patient's letter handed over at desk

A patient with the same surname as a diabetic patient was given a finger-prick glucose test intended for the other patient. The result was normal and no insulin was given. Patient was upset by the unnecessary procedure.
Apology given, same-surname alert added to the whiteboard.
Glucose test performed on patient with same surname
Midwife noticed that a baby's name band had the mother's previous surname and corrected it before the baby was taken for the newborn screening test.
Band reprinted and checked against the mother's band.
Newborn name band showed old surname
At the sign-in check, the scrub nurse noticed that the consent form was for a left knee and the list showed a right knee. The surgeon clarified the side with the patient before anaesthesia.
Consent form corrected and signed again, list updated.
Consent form side did not match theatre list
A urine sample was received in an unlabelled container delivered by a porter. It was traced back to the ward by process of elimination and a repeat was requested.
Repeat sample collected, ward reminded about labelling at the bedside.
Unlabelled urine sample traced back to ward
Stage 1 pressure area on the heel found at the morning skin check on a patient with limited movement after a stroke. Turning chart showed two missed turns overnight.
Heel offloaded with a boot, turning schedule restarted, tissue viability nurse informed.
Stage 1 heel pressure area after missed turns
Stage 2 sacral pressure injury identified on day nine of ventilation in a patient who could not be turned fully because of unstable blood pressure.
Dressings applied, pressure-relieving mattress upgraded, tissue viability review and family informed.
Stage 2 sacral injury during prolonged ventilation
A cannula bandage left too tight caused a small pressure sore on the patient's wrist, found when the dressing was changed.
Bandage replaced, area dressed, cannula site changed.
Tight cannula bandage causing wrist pressure sore

On admission an existing sacral pressure area was recorded as new by the ward team because the transfer form from the other facility did not list it. Corrected after the photo record from the referral was found.
Admission skin assessment updated, referring facility contacted.
Pre-existing pressure area recorded as new on admission
Elderly patient waited on a trolley for nearly nine hours before a bed was available and had a red patch on the sacrum on arrival at the ward.
Pressure-relieving cushion applied, skin checked every two hours, flagged to bed management.
Redness on sacrum after nine-hour trolley wait
Nurse noticed that the turning chart for bed 8 was ticked in advance. She checked the patient and found the position unchanged for five hours, and turned him before any skin damage.
Patient repositioned, ward manager informed, chart practice reviewed.
Turning chart ticked in advance, patient not turned for five hours
A patient wearing anti-embolism stockings developed a blister on the right heel which was not noticed for two days because stockings were not removed for skin checks.
Stockings removed, heel dressed and checks added to the daily care plan.
Blister under anti-embolism stockings missed for two days

Infusion pump alarmed with an occlusion message that was silenced twice by a nurse who assumed it was a kinked line. On the third alarm the biomedical team found a faulty pressure sensor and replaced the pump. No patient effect.
Pump removed from service, biomedical engineering review.
Defibrillator pads in the resuscitation trolley were found to be one month past their expiry date during the daily check. Replaced before use.
Pads replaced and the trolley checklist updated to include expiry dates.
Expired defibrillator pads in resus trolley
Hospital bed lost its brake on a sloped bay and slowly moved while the patient was getting in. The patient held the rail and was not hurt.
Bed taken out of service and tagged, bay inspected.
Bed brake failure on sloped bay
A metal oxygen cylinder was brought into the MRI scan room by a ward porter who had not been briefed. The radiographer stopped him at the door before it could be attracted to the magnet.
Cylinder replaced with an MRI-safe type, porter briefed, signage improved at the door.
Metal oxygen cylinder stopped at MRI room entrance
Diathermy plate cable showed a fault during an operation and the surgeon changed to another unit. No burn occurred.
Unit tagged and sent for repair, surgery continued.
Faulty diathermy plate cable replaced mid-operation
The analyser quality control failed at 07:15 but results for four patients were released before the failure was reviewed. Results were rechecked and none changed by more than the acceptable range.
Patients' results re-run, analyser recalibrated, release process tightened.
Results released before quality control failure was reviewed
Alarm on the infant warmer failed to sound during a routine test. The test was done at the start of shift so the unit was replaced before a baby was placed in it.
Infant warmer alarm failed on routine test
The ear thermometer gave readings 2 degrees lower than expected across several patients. Calibration was found to be out and the unit replaced.
Thermometer reading low due to calibration drift
A suction unit checked at the start of the shift did not generate enough vacuum. It was replaced from the spare stock and sent for service.
Unit replaced and sent to biomedical engineering.
Suction unit with low vacuum found at shift check
Patient developed redness and warmth around a peripheral cannula on day four. Cannula had no date label and was removed late. Treated with oral antibiotics.
Cannula removed, site swabbed, antibiotics prescribed, cannula date labels audited.
Cannula site infection on an undated line
Central line bloodstream infection confirmed on day eleven in a ventilated patient. Insertion checklist was complete but line dressing had been found loose on two checks.
Line removed, antibiotics changed, infection control review, family informed.
A relative entered an isolation room without gown or gloves while the nurse was away from the door. Nurse noticed on return and gave instruction and PPE.
Visitor reminded about precautions, signage on the door enlarged.
Visitor entered isolation room without protective equipment
A sterile instrument tray was opened and found to have an indicator strip that had not changed colour. The tray was discarded and replaced and the batch quarantined.
Tray replaced, sterilisation department notified and batch reviewed.
Sterility indicator not changed on opened instrument tray
A patient with a rash and fever consistent with chickenpox sat in the main waiting room for 20 minutes before being identified. Triage questions on exposure were not asked at the desk.
Patient moved to an isolation room and staff immunity checked.
Possible chickenpox patient in waiting room for 20 minutes
Mother developed a superficial wound infection at her caesarean site that was picked up at the day-seven check. Wound care advice at discharge had been given in English only.
Antibiotics started, wound care leaflet provided in Arabic.
Caesarean wound infection after leaflet only in English
Hand hygiene observation showed that a phlebotomist was moving between patients without cleaning hands. Reminded at the time and the area manager informed.
Immediate feedback and refresher session arranged.
Hand hygiene missed between patients in phlebotomy
Alcohol hand rub dispensers on the corridor were found empty on two consecutive rounds. Housekeeping had not been told the refill schedule.
Dispensers refilled, refill rota created with housekeeping.
Empty hand rub dispensers on the Ward 2 corridor

At the peak of the Tuesday morning clinic an elderly man with chest pain sat in the overcrowded OPD waiting area for 40 minutes before a passing nurse noticed him. He was taken to Emergency and was treated without lasting harm. The queue had no triage nurse at the time.
Patient transferred to Emergency immediately, charge nurse and OPD head informed.
Chest pain patient waited 40 minutes in crowded OPD queue
Handover sheet for the night shift was missing the isolation status for bed 12, and a new nurse took the patient to the day room before the error was spotted.
Patient returned to room, handover template updated.
Isolation status missing from handover sheet
A patient left the Emergency department without being seen after waiting more than three hours. Nurse tried to reach him by phone and he later returned the next morning.
Patient seen on return, wait time review requested.
Patient left Emergency after three-hour wait

sentinel.title: Inpatient fall with hip fracture
sentinel.description: A 78-year-old patient on Ward 3 was found on the floor beside her bed at 02:15 with pain in the right hip. She had been assessed as low falls risk on admission and the bed alarm was not in use. X-ray confirmed a displaced hip fracture and she was transferred to theatre for surgery.
sentinel.immediate_action: Medical review, analgesia and X-ray, orthopaedic team called, family informed by the consultant, bed and area secured for review.
facts: Patient settled for the night after evening medication, including a sedating antihistamine for itching.
Hourly rounding completed, patient asleep. Bed alarm not in use. Call bell within reach.
Night shift reduced to two nurses for 24 beds after one colleague was redeployed to the Emergency department.
Round due. Delayed by an unwell patient in bed 20.
Healthcare assistant heard a noise and found the patient on the floor beside the bed, awake and complaining of right hip pain.
Duty doctor reviewed. X-ray requested urgently. Orthopaedics informed.
X-ray confirmed displaced neck-of-femur fracture. Consent discussion with family started.

people: Two nurses covering 24 beds overnight after a redeployment
Rounding delayed by an unwell patient in bed 20
process: Falls risk assessed as low on admission and not repeated after new sedating medication
No trigger to reassess after a change in medication
equipment: Bed alarm available but not switched on
environment: Room dimly lit at night, path from bed to bathroom 4 metres
communication: Handover did not mention the patient's evening sedative
policy: Falls policy requires reassessment only at 72 hours or after a fall

whys: Why did the patient fall? She got up alone at night to go to the bathroom while drowsy.
Why was she drowsy and unattended? A sedating antihistamine was given at 22:40 and rounding was delayed.
Why was rounding delayed? Two nurses were covering 24 beds and one was with an unwell patient.
Why was the falls risk not reassessed after the new medication? The policy does not require reassessment when a sedating drug is started.
Why was staffing reduced? Redeployment to the Emergency department has no minimum safe level for the ward.
sentinel.root_cause: The falls policy does not require reassessment of falls risk when a sedating drug is started, and overnight redeployment can reduce Ward 3 below a safe staffing level, so a drowsy low-risk patient was left without a bed alarm or timely rounding.
capas: Add a falls risk reassessment prompt to the medication chart whenever a sedating or blood-pressure-lowering drug is started.
Switch on bed alarms for every patient on a new sedating drug for the first 24 hours.
Set a minimum overnight staffing level for medical wards that cannot be breached by redeployment without a duty manager decision.
Add night-time lighting along the path from bed to bathroom in Ward 3 bays.

falls: Reinforce the falls risk assessment at admission and after any change in medication or condition.
Add bed-exit alarm checks to the start-of-shift equipment round.
Remove obstacles and place call bells and walking aids within reach during every round.
Provide non-slip footwear to patients assessed at moderate or high falls risk.
Place wet-floor signs immediately and clear spills within five minutes.
medication: Separate look-alike and sound-alike medicines in storage and add shelf labels.
Introduce an independent double-check for high-risk infusions at every handover.
Make weight a required field before paediatric prescriptions can be signed.
Require the allergy band to be checked against the chart before any new antibiotic is given.
Run a teaching session on documenting administration immediately after giving each dose.
patient_identification: Remind staff to use two identifiers at every sample collection and transfusion.
Add a same-name alert flag to booking lists and whiteboards.
Print wristbands at admission and check them at every transfer.
Review the discharge letter handing process so that the name and date of birth are read back at the desk.
pressure_injury: Complete a skin assessment within six hours of admission and record it with a photo.
Audit turning charts weekly and give feedback to ward managers.
Review pressure-relieving mattress availability for the ward and ICU.
Check skin under stockings, bandages and devices at least once per shift.
equipment: Add expiry dates and function checks to the daily resuscitation trolley list.
Quarantine and tag faulty equipment, and log it with biomedical engineering the same day.
Brief all porters and visitors on MRI-safe equipment at the scanner entrance.
Include alarm tests in the start-of-shift check for every infant warmer and infusion pump.
infection: Date-label every peripheral cannula and review the need for it every 24 hours.
Audit hand hygiene using the five moments and share the results with the ward.
Refill hand rub dispensers on a published rota agreed with housekeeping.
Use the central line insertion and maintenance bundle with a daily dressing check.
other: Add a peak-hour triage nurse to the OPD waiting area and re-space clinic start times.
Update the handover template so that isolation status cannot be left blank.

root_causes.falls: The patient attempted to mobilise without help because the call bell was not used and the bed alarm was off.
root_causes.medication: A look-alike or unchecked step at administration was not caught because the independent check was not done at that point.
root_causes.patient_identification: The two-identifier check was skipped or rushed at the point of care.
root_causes.pressure_injury: Repositioning was delayed or not recorded as scheduled.
root_causes.equipment: A scheduled check did not detect the fault before use.
root_causes.infection: A step in the standard infection control bundle was missed or delayed.
root_causes.other: The process had no safeguard at peak times.
